Can someone explain to me why knives mostly have one cutting side?

Double-edged blades need to have a thick central spine for strength; this makes for a thick grind angle from the spine to the edge. A single-edge blade of the same size would have a grind that's half as thick, which allows it to cut much better.

One cutting edge results in a stronger blade, better suited to rough work. A two-sided blade is thinner. It breaks more easily, but is better suited to slide between someone's ribs. Form dictates function, but it's always a compromise.
